intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam was conducted on 6 October 2026 across three shifts. Candidates reported a range of overall difficulty levels, from Easy to Difficult, with most describing the paper as Moderate. Good attempts varied by shift, roughly between 20 and 92 out of 100, but these figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts before publishing final results. Common observations included time pressure from sectional timers and lengthy questions, especially in Quantitative Aptitude and English.

shifts.summary: Candidates reported overall difficulty ranging from Easy to Difficult, with most labeling it Moderate. Good attempts varied between 70 and 92 out of 100. Reasoning was generally easy, while Quant had mixed difficulty and English was mostly easy. Time pressure from sectional timers and lengthy questions was a common issue.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: A few long questions caused time pressure; some puzzle and number‑series questions were skipped. Slog questions were lengthy and tricky. Coding‑decoding and analogy items were present but not overly hard.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: Questions were factual; options often needed deeper knowledge. Current affairs focused on one‑liners and older events. GK difficulty ranged from easy to moderate.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Time shortage on lengthy calculations; many advanced arithmetic and mensuration items. Some sections had heavy advanced math weightage causing pressure.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Reading comprehension passages were easy to moderate. Spelling and idiom questions added some difficulty.

shifts.summary: The shift 2 paper was seen as generally easy to moderate overall, with candidates attempting around 70–86.5 out of 100. Reasoning was mostly easy with good attempts near 24‑25 questions. Quantitative section caused time pressure, difficulty ranged widely and attempts were about 16–18.6 questions. English had lengthier passages and vocabulary focus, with attempts around 23.5. General Awareness leaned towards static GK.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Most questions were statement based, with some lengthy address type and coding‑decoding or analogy. Candidates reported time‑consuming questions and lower attempts.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: Shift had more static GK and few current‑affairs questions.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Sectional timer made math tough; questions were calculative and advanced, many candidates could not finish all 25 questions.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Paper was lengthier with each question attached to a passage, including two comprehensive passages. Vocabulary was heavy and grammar revision was needed.

shifts.summary: The shift was reported as Easy by RealMocks and Difficult by SSC, giving an overall Easy to Difficult rating. Candidates attempted well between 20 and 85 questions across papers. Reasoning was moderate to easy with time pressure noted. GA and Quant showed mixed difficulty levels, while English ranged from easy to difficult. Vocabulary and error‑detection were highlighted in English.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty levels were reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 6 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was described as Moderate, Shift 2 as Easy to Moderate, and Shift 3 as Easy to Difficult, reflecting differing perceptions among candidates.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates attempt on average across the shifts on 6 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reported good attempts ranged from about 20 to 92 questions out of 100, depending on the shift and section.

faqs.q: Which sections caused the most time pressure for candidates on 6 October 2026?
faqs.a: Time pressure was most frequently mentioned for the Quantitative Aptitude section and for English passages, especially where sectional timers were active.

faqs.q: How did the difficulty of Quantitative Aptitude vary across the shifts on 6 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative Aptitude was reported as mixed in Shift 1, caused notable time pressure in Shift 2, and showed mixed difficulty in Shift 3.

faqs.q: Are the reported attempt figures for 6 October 2026 final, or does SSC adjust them?
faqs.a: The figures are unofficial; SSC normalises scores across shifts before releasing the official results.
